answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making each identity grow one continuous thread of useful work from a shared kernel of trust. A newcomer starts with a bare kernel and must complete a long, publicly auditable thread of small jobs, each checked by different established peers, before it can transact. The thread cannot be split, copied, or bought: a copper coin buys a day of compute, not a history. Faking ten identities means building ten full threads of real work, so the cost of forgery grows with every fake while honest agents pay it only once.
